BiblicalUsage: Shabats is entanglement, anguish, and it holds the dying Saul on Gilboa: stand, I pray thee, upon me, and slay me, for anguish is come upon me, because my life is yet whole in me.
TheologicalSignificance: What I take from this is that Saul's end is entanglement itself — caught between life and death, and asking another man to finish it.
